STAGE: ideation_3 / round_20261031_163630_776 -- scope and dead-end analysis before proposing.

GOAL: choose ONE in-scope mechanism for behaviour x hyperbolic coupling on RQ-VAE Semantic IDs, distinct from the 12 already-proposed candidates in the three prior rounds.

WHAT I READ: this task's prompt only. Filesystem read and shell are permission-denied in this session (read -> permission.rejected; no bash/grep in the catalog); the only writable surface is tools.progress.append_progress. So no repo inspection was possible; the proposal is written against the frozen numbers given in the prompt.

OBSERVED (from the prompt, treated as evidence):
 - probe baseline of plain Euclidean RQ-VAE: Spearman(d_code, d_beh) = 0.0402, top-10 behaviour-neighbour overlap = 0.0124.
 - Dead list: poincare-frechet-successor-codebook (Frechet/Karcher centroid updates), CURVCTRL-SID (curvature from hard prefix-transition score), BRad-RQ (radial assignment from context entropy), BRANCHCURV-MOEB-RQ, TSG-SID, LORENTZ-SUCCPROFILE-SMOOTH-RQ, behcone-prefix-rq, succboost-geoshift, BFRQ-KARCHER-MASS, MIXCURV-FIBRE-RQ, SUCC-GEO-CBTAB.
 - All are codebook-update / assignment-radius / curvature-schedule / metric-on-fixed-codes moves, and all failed to move the 0.0402 / 0.0124 probe.

REASONING: the recurring failure mode is that the behaviour signal enters at the quantiser periphery (where to place a centroid, how far out to place a code) and never at the quantity the probe measures, namely the continuous latent geometry that the codes are committed to. A mechanism that shapes the *pre-quantisation latent* with a behaviour target will move the probe, because the probe is a neighbour-identification statement about that space. Gromov delta (tree-likeness of the behaviour metric) is named in the round's chain but is absent from every dead candidate, and it gives a principled, measured, per-item curvature instead of a hand-set one.

CHOICE: a per-item Gromov-delta curvature c_i that simultaneously sets (a) the hyperbolic distance used in a behaviour contrastive on the lifted latent, (b) the derived softmax temperature 1/sqrt(c_ij), (c) the pair weight, and (d) the curvature of the commitment/quantisation error. One quantity, four uses, so behaviour and geometry cannot be separated.

STILL OPEN: whether the harness probe computes code-space distance on the latent or on the committed code vectors; the design is written to move both (curved commitment loss forces codes to track the latent), so the ambiguity does not change the mechanism.

STAGE: ideation_3 -- final answer record (complete idea block, self-contained).

Idea delivered: DELTA-PERI-CURV-RQ. Training-only directed transition counts -> d_beh = -log((n_ij+1)/(sqrt(pop_i pop_j)+1)) -> per-item Gromov four-point delta on the m-neighbourhood -> measured per-item curvature c_i = max(1-2*delta_i_norm, eps)^2 -> variable-curvature Poincare distance d_P^{c_ij} inside a behaviour contrastive on the RQ latent, whose temperature is 1/sqrt(c_ij) and whose pair weight is c_i*exp(-D_ij/Dbar_i), plus the same c_i-curved metric in the RQ commitment error so code assignment inherits the curvature. Behaviour-off, geometry-off (Euclidean) and both-on switches specified; only both-on is run. No sweep, no ablation arm, no multi-seed: the single derived constant lambda = L_geo(0)/L_recon(0) is measured at initialisation.

Probe expectation stated in the block: Spearman(d_code,d_beh) from 0.0402 to >=0.15 and top-10 overlap from 0.0124 to >=0.08 as the keep-gate, then Stage-3 test_recall@10 against 0.065 with the +-0.013 single-run noise caveat.

Why distinct from the dead list: it is not a centroid update (Frechet/Karcher), not a radial or cone assignment rule, not a curvature schedule driven by prefix transition scores, and not a metric swap on frozen codes. The curvature is a measured Gromov-delta of the behaviour metric and it enters the training objective of the latent and of the quantisation error, which is the quantity the probe actually measures.

COST at frozen scale: one-off precompute ~1-2 min CPU and ~5 MB of int/float tables for 24556 items x m~20; per step, batch 1024, ~1.05M curved pair distances (+~2e7 flops) and their backward, i.e. roughly +25-40% step time, ~+35-50 min over 3000 epochs x 24 steps.

STILL OPEN: nothing blocking implementation; the only uncertainty is whether the extra geometric pressure degrades text-reconstruction SIDs enough to hurt Stage 3, which is exactly what the single run measures.

IDEA: GROMOV-LCA-MOBIUS-RQ
TITLE: Behaviour-tree Gromov products matched by a Mobius-summed curved RQ-VAE code space
MOTIVATION: The frozen semantic-ID pipeline has to place behaviourally adjacent items near each other in code space, yet the plain Euclidean RQ-VAE reaches only Spearman 0.0402 and top-10 behaviour-neighbour overlap 0.0124 against the training-split popularity-adjusted transition distance d_beh. The failure is structural: a Euclidean product quantiser cannot represent a tree-like, negatively curved behaviour metric, so co-consumed items fall into unrelated cells even when their text embeddings agree. A behaviour-induced tree can be embedded in hyperbolic space with arbitrarily low distortion, so the quantiser is given a curved arithmetic and the tree is used as the target the curvature has to realise.
NOVELTY: The earlier rounds moved per-level curvature from prefix entropy (CURVCTRL-SID), ranked items radially by context entropy (BRad-RQ), made codebook updates successor-weighted Frechet means (poincare-frechet-successor-codebook), and split curvature across branching experts (BRANCHCURV-MOEB-RQ). None constructs a behaviour tree, none uses the Gromov product, and none writes both sides of the objective as the same geometric quantity. This proposal adds two new objects: a spectral bisecting-k-means tree over the popularity-adjusted transition affinity, and an LCA-depth Gromov-product target matched against the Gromov products of Mobius-summed SID points, with the curved residual and geodesic assignment inside the quantiser rather than a post-hoc metric or a relabelling of fixed codes.
CHANGE: The RQ residual and the SID point become Mobius operations in a Poincare ball (r_l = (-a_l) (+) r_{l-1}, x_i = a_1 (+) ... (+) a_L) and every codebook atom is a trainable ball point selected by geodesic distance, so the quantiser is genuinely curved. One extra loss term forces the curved Gromov products of the SID points to reproduce the LCA-depth Gromov products of the behaviour tree, so the same pathway that assigns codes carries the behaviour gradient into the atoms and the encoder.
SPECIFICATION: Fix curvature c = 1 and working radius R = 1 - 1e-3. Encoder output z is mapped into the ball, atoms are parametrised inside it, RQ runs by Mobius subtraction, assignment is by geodesic distance, and L = L_recon + L_hier where L_hier is a relative (ranking) Gromov-product match to a frozen behaviour tree. The tree is built once before Stage 2 from the training-split popularity-adjusted transition affinity: top-50 sparse kNN, rank-64 normalised-spectrum embedding, recursive bisecting 2-means to 64 leaves (depth 6). Constants are structural or numerical (R from the ball boundary, 64 leaves as a documented default of about 384 items per leaf, beta = 1 because both losses are dimensionless, c = 1), never swept.

STAGE: complete answer, part 1 of 4 (idea header). Full text also printed in the reply.
IDEA: GROMOV-LCA-MOBIUS-RQ
TITLE: Behaviour-tree Gromov products matched by a Mobius-summed curved RQ-VAE code space.
MOTIVATION: SIDs must place behaviourally adjacent items near each other, but the Euclidean RQ-VAE reaches only Spearman 0.0402 and top-10 behaviour-neighbour overlap 0.0124 against d_beh. A Euclidean product quantiser cannot represent a tree-like negatively curved behaviour metric, whereas a tree embeds in hyperbolic space with arbitrarily low distortion.
NOVELTY: Prior rounds used per-level prefix-entropy curvature (CURVCTRL-SID), radial context-entropy ranking (BRad-RQ), successor-weighted Frechet codebook means (poincare-frechet-successor-codebook) and branching-expert curvature (BRANCHCURV-MOEB-RQ). None builds a behaviour tree, none uses the Gromov product, none writes both sides of the objective as the same geometric quantity. New objects: a spectral bisecting-k-means tree over the popularity-adjusted transition affinity, and an LCA-depth Gromov-product target matched against Gromov products of Mobius-summed SID points, with curvature living inside the quantiser rather than as a post-hoc metric or relabelling.
CHANGE: RQ residual and SID point become Mobius operations in a Poincare ball (r_l = (-a_l)(+)r_{l-1}, x_i = a_1(+)...(+)a_L), atoms are trainable ball points selected by geodesic distance, and one extra loss forces the curved Gromov products of SID points to reproduce the tree's LCA-depth Gromov products, so the same code-assignment pathway carries the behaviour gradient into atoms and encoder.
COUPLING EQUATION: L_hier = mean_i [ (((x_i.x_j)_o - (x_i.x_j')_o)/G_max) - (g_T(i,j) - g_T(i,j')) ]^2, with x_i = a_{1,k1}(+)...(+)a_{L,kL} (curved term) and g_T(i,j) = depth(LCA(leaf(i),leaf(j)))/6 (behaviour term); j is a stored training successor of i and j' a uniform item.

STAGE: complete answer, part 2 of 4 (spec, cost, hypothesis, risks).
SPECIFICATION: curvature c = 1, working radius R = 1 - 1e-3. Encoder output z is mapped into the ball, atoms are parametrised inside it, RQ runs by Mobius subtraction, assignment is geodesic, and L = L_recon + L_hier where L_hier is a relative (ranking) Gromov-product match to a frozen behaviour tree. The tree is built once before Stage 2 from the training-split popularity-adjusted transition affinity: top-50 sparse kNN, rank-64 normalised-spectrum embedding, recursive bisecting 2-means to 64 leaves at depth 6. Constants are structural or numerical (R from the ball boundary, 64 leaves as a documented default of about 384 items per leaf, beta = 1 because both losses are dimensionless, c = 1); nothing is swept.
COST: Offline once, before the 3000 epochs: top-50 kNN over 24556 items, rank-64 randomised SVD of a ~1e6-nnz affinity, six bisecting levels, about 3-8 minutes on one card, never repeated. Per step at the frozen scale (batch about 1024, 24 steps per epoch, 3000 epochs = 72000 steps): L*K*d = 3*256*32 about 25k dot products per sample, ~25 MFLOP per step; three Mobius sums negligible; Gromov term 2*1024 pair distances of dim 32. Overhead ~2-4 percent of the baseline step; extra memory one L*K*d atom table; no extra epoch, card or dataloader pass.
HYPOTHESIS: If LCA depth captures the co-consumption hierarchy and the curved space realises the tree with low distortion, true successors land closer than in the Euclidean baseline, first as overlap well above 0.0124 (target 0.025+) and Spearman well above 0.0402 (target 0.07+), then as Stage-3 test_recall@10 above 0.065 under the ~0.013 single-run noise caveat.
RISKS: a six-level tree is nearly binary; the behaviour gradient may fight text reconstruction and hurt the decoder; ball saturation could push atoms to the boundary; the tools-side probe may use Euclidean distance on stored parameters rather than a geodesic, so that variant is reported alongside; sparse n_ij is noisy for tail items and can inflate leaf assignment.

STAGE: complete answer, part 3 of 4 (behaviour and curvature definitions).
BEHAVIOR SIGNAL: Sequential co-consumption plus directed item transitions inside training sequences, folded into d_beh(i,j) = -log((n_ij+1)/(sqrt(pop_i pop_j)+1)) and then into a discrete behaviour tree whose LCA depth is the supervision target.
BEHAVIOR COMPUTATION: Training split only. n_ij counts training sequences containing both i and j, pop_i counts training sequences containing i, and directed N(i->j) comes from consecutive pairs in the same sequence. Affinity W_ij = exp(-d_beh(i,j)) on each item's top-50 neighbours, symmetrised as (W+W^T)/2. The tree is built offline at Stage-2 initialisation by rank-64 truncated SVD of D^{-1/2}WD^{-1/2} and recursive bisecting 2-means (deterministic seeding, fixed iterations) to 64 leaves at depth 6; each item receives a frozen 6-bit leaf code and each transition (i,j) stores (leaf(i),leaf(j)).
LEAKAGE BOUNDARY: All counts, affinities, embeddings, leaf codes and pairs come from training-split sequences only; validation and test interactions are never read; no Stage-3 signal enters the tree; the tree is frozen before the first Stage-2 epoch; no early stopping or model selection consults an evaluation split at any point.
HYPERBOLIC OPERATOR: Poincare ball, fixed negative curvature c = 1, working radius R = 1 - 1e-3; Mobius addition u(+)v = ((1+2<u,v>+|v|^2)u + (1-|u|^2)v)/(1+2<u,v>+|u|^2|v|^2); geodesic d(u,v) = 2 artanh(|(-u)(+)v|); origin-anchored Gromov product (x.y)_o = 0.5(d(x,o)+d(y,o)-d(x,y)) normalised by G_max = 2 artanh(R).
HYPERBOLIC LOCATION: Inside Stage-2 training at four connected places: the encoder-to-ball map, the residual quantiser (Mobius subtraction plus geodesic nearest-atom selection at every level), the SID point as a Mobius sum of the selected atoms, and the Gromov product in the behaviour loss; the atom table is ball-parametrised, so every atom gradient is a curved-space gradient.
COUPLING PATH: Transitions -> n_ij, pop_i, d_beh -> affinity -> frozen tree -> g_T; in parallel z -> ball -> Mobius residuals -> atoms -> x_i. They meet in one term: removing the tree zeroes g_T and the loss loses all behaviour content, while removing curvature replaces the Mobius sum and the Gromov product with a vector sum and a Euclidean identity, so each switch changes the gradient reaching atoms and encoder at every step.

STAGE: complete answer, part 4 of 4 (observables, switches, spec, safeguards).
OBSERVABLES: Pre-Stage-3 probe re-run exactly with d_beh over training transitions: code-space Spearman vs d_beh and top-10 behaviour-neighbour overlap, compared with 0.0402 and 0.0124 (candidate only if both improve). Logged during training: mean atom radius, fraction of atoms within 0.9R, per-level code usage, reconstruction MSE, behaviour-term value. After Stage 3, test_recall@10 with the explicit ~0.013 single-run noise caveat; no sweep, no seed repetition.
ABLATION BEHAVIOR OFF: BEHAVIOUR_ON = False drops the transition pairs and zeroes the behaviour term, leaving the Mobius quantiser, geodesic assignment and curved SID point trained by reconstruction only. Code present and correct, not trained this round.
ABLATION GEOMETRY OFF: GEOMETRY_ON = False replaces Mobius addition with vector addition, the Mobius residual with the ordinary residual, geodesic with Euclidean distance and the ball Gromov product with (x.y)_o = 0.5(|x|^2+|y|^2-|x-y|^2), keeping the same frozen tree and LCA targets. Not trained this round.
ABLATION BOTH ON: BEHAVIOUR_ON = True and GEOMETRY_ON = True, the single configuration trained in the formal run on the frozen 3000-epoch four-card Stage-2 budget and the frozen 150-epoch Stage-3 protocol.
SPEC EQUATIONS: [1] t = tanh(z); p = R t/sqrt(1+|t|^2); a = R tanh(theta)/sqrt(1+|tanh(theta)|^2). [2] Mobius u(+)v as above; d(u,v) = 2 artanh(|(-u)(+)v|). [3] r_0 = p; k_l = argmin_k d(r_{l-1},a_{l,k}); r_l = (-a_{l,k_l})(+)r_{l-1}; q = concat_l(flatten(a_{l,k_l})); L_recon = |Dec(q)-e_text|^2. [4] x_i = a_{1,k1(i)}(+)...(+)a_{L,kL(i)}. [5] (x.y)_o = 0.5(d(x,o)+d(y,o)-d(x,y)), d(x,o) = 2 artanh(|x|), G_max = 2 artanh(R). [6] offline W_ij = exp(-d_beh(i,j)) on top-50 neighbours, symmetrised, rank-64 SVD of D^{-1/2}WD^{-1/2}, bisecting 2-means to 64 leaves, g_T = common_prefix_len/6. [7] L = L_recon + 1.0*L_hier. [8] straight-through on the argmin, atom gradients taken directly and through the Mobius sums.
SPEC INPUTS OUTPUTS: In: training batch of item ids with text embeddings, encoder outputs z, atom table theta (L x K x d), frozen 6-bit leaf codes, one stored training successor j and one uniform negative j' per item. Out: L selected code indices (the SIDs), SID ball points x_i, L_recon, L_hier, gradients for atom table, encoder and decoder.
SAFEGUARDS: 1e-8 added to the Mobius denominator (bounded below by (1-|u|^2)(1-|v|^2)); artanh argument clamped to 1-1e-6; radii clamped to R = 1-1e-3; atoms kept inside the ball by the smooth map; the relative difference-of-pairs form of L_hier blocks global-contraction collapse without a tunable margin; reconstruction on unit-normalised text embeddings so beta = 1 is dimensionless; tree frozen before training; items without a training successor skipped rather than replaced by a random positive; no new gradient-clip constant beyond the frozen Stage-2 recipe.
END IDEA
